title: Texas's 16th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 16th Congressional District pits four-term Democratic incumbent Veronica Escobar against Republican nominee Adam Bauman. The district covers most of El Paso County and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+11, making it one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in Texas. Escobar, first elected in 2018 as one of the first Latina congresswomen from Texas, is seeking a fifth term in a district that has not elected a Republican since 1962. The race is rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report, and national Republican leaders have not listed TX-16 among seats they plan to seriously contest.
polling_note: No district-specific public opinion polls were found for this race. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D' as of February 2025.

candidates.name: Veronica Escobar
candidates.summary: Veronica Escobar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 16th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. She previously served as El Paso County Judge (2011-2017) and El Paso County Commissioner (2006-2010). Escobar serves on the House Armed Services and Judiciary Committees and was one of four co-chairs of the 2024 Democratic National Convention.

candidates.name: Adam Bauman
candidates.summary: Adam Bauman is the Republican nominee for Texas's 16th Congressional District, having won the GOP primary runoff on May 26, 2026, with 69% of the vote. He is a former U.S. Border Patrol agent who served on the elite Border Patrol Tactical Team (BORTAC) and is a U.S. Navy Special Warfare Combatant Crewman (SWCC) veteran. Bauman runs a tactical canine business and has campaigned on border security, lower property taxes, and veterans' issues.
